title: Measurability of the Gaussian indicator average
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$. The function $x\mapsto\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ is measurable, where $\gamma_n$ is the standard Gaussian product measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. For measurable $A$ and every real $\theta$, the function $u_\theta$ is measurable.
